diagrams.title: From Signed Merchant to Audited Residual
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages separate payment volume from operator earnings.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The revenue basis is retained ISO residuals, gateway markups, and ATM surcharge shares. Merchant settlement funds and ATM vault cash are excluded. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment follows the actual contracts; this model uses the specified retained basis.
diagrams.caption: Own the contract, verify the boarding decision, and reconcile the retained payment before treating an account as productive.

stages.label: Source and qualify
stages.detail: Capture merchant category, ownership, statements, refund patterns, venue traffic, and placement rights in IRIS CRM; reject prohibited activity before quoting.

stages.label: Price the retained spread
stages.value: Model Schedule A and venue shares
stages.detail: Calculate residuals after processor deductions and ATM venue shares; document gateway markup, minimums, clawbacks, reserve exposure, and residual assignment rights.

stages.label: Submit transparent underwriting
stages.detail: Submit accurate ownership, merchant category, websites, fulfillment terms, and processing history. Never split transactions across MIDs to conceal risk or thresholds.

stages.label: Activate and monitor
stages.detail: Test debit exclusions and credit-price presentation; configure supported Verifi RDR or Ethoca workflows, ATM fee election, remote telemetry, and vault-cash alerts.

stages.label: Audit and retain
stages.detail: Reconcile IRIS CRM residual imports against Schedule A and sponsor statements; investigate missing MIDs, rate compression, surcharge deductions, attrition, and cash variances.

diagrams.title: A Nested Merchant Acquisition Cohort
diagrams.subtitle: 400 prospects become 25 active merchants over an illustrative 120 days.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage; these are planning counts, not observed conversion results. First deal timing remains 1–4 months. The separate ATM portfolio is excluded from this funnel.
diagrams.caption: At steady state, 25 merchants retaining $15,000 annually each contribute $375,000; ten separately sourced ATM venues retaining $7,000 each complete the $445,000 Base revenue case.

stages.label: Named prospects
stages.detail: Record identifiable businesses with permitted categories, reachable decision-makers, serviceable locations, and an explicit reason to reconsider their existing processing arrangement.

stages.label: Qualified statement audits
stages.detail: Obtain authorized statements and confirm ownership, processing needs, renewal timing, current pricing, and risk fit before allocating proposal effort.

stages.label: Documented proposals
stages.detail: Present itemized pricing and service terms; calculate retained contribution after upstream deductions rather than treating interchange or merchant settlement as revenue.

stages.label: Complete sponsor submissions
stages.detail: Submit complete applications with genuine business activity, required evidence, and disclosed processing history; submission does not imply sponsor acceptance.

stages.label: Active retained accounts
stages.detail: Count only live accounts with reconciled processing. Illustrative annual yield is $500,000 monthly merchant volume times 12 times a 0.25% retained spread, or $15,000.

diagrams.title: Base Case: $445,000 Revenue to $189,125 Owner Profit
diagrams.subtitle: Four expense deductions reconcile exactly to a 42.5% annual net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: USD annually. The first and last bars are absolute totals; the four intervening bars are negative deltas. Expense allocations are illustrative and reconcile to the canonical scorecard. Revenue is already net of upstream retained-share deductions.

stages.label: Retained operator revenue
stages.detail: Base revenue comprises $375,000 retained merchant and gateway income plus $70,000 retained ATM surcharge income. Merchant card volume and vault cash contribute zero revenue.

stages.label: Acquisition commissions
stages.detail: Pay operator-side referral and sales compensation under documented schedules. These costs are distinct from processor and venue shares already removed from revenue.

stages.label: Contract servicing
stages.detail: Fund contractor boarding, residual auditing, dispute operations, and ATM field-service work; the full-time owner's compensation is not deducted again from owner profit.

stages.label: Fixed operating overhead
stages.detail: Budget CRM, telemetry, insurance, equipment leases, bookkeeping, and administration. Average fixed overhead is $4,989.58 monthly; total expenses also include variable costs.

stages.label: Loss and remediation expense
stages.detail: Model operator-borne losses and remediation costs under the relevant contracts. Restricted reserve deposits are not automatically expenses, and recoverable vault cash is excluded.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.detail: Canonical checks: Conservative $90,000 times 30% equals $27,000; Base $445,000 times 42.5% equals $189,125; Scaled $800,000 times 55% equals $440,000.

diagrams.title: Retained Yield by Merchant Segment and Payment Rail
diagrams.subtitle: Illustrative operator dollars retained per 1,000 successful payment events.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Card examples assume a $50 average ticket. Gateway yield is a separate component, not an additional merchant cohort. ATM events are withdrawals, not purchases; differing event economics prevent direct conclusions about account profitability. Bars are not additive.
diagrams.caption: Price retained yield after upstream splits, then subtract operator acquisition, servicing, and loss costs.

stages.label: Card-present retail residual
stages.detail: One thousand $50 purchases produce $50,000 merchant volume; a 24-basis-point retained residual produces $120 before operator expenses, without assuming debit surcharges.

stages.label: Restaurant processing residual
stages.detail: A 32-basis-point retained residual on $50,000 merchant volume produces $160; verify tip adjustments, funding timing, terminal support, and rate-matching exposure.

stages.label: Gateway transaction markup
stages.detail: A $0.09 retained gateway markup produces $90 across 1,000 transactions; deduct the upstream gateway charge before measuring this component and avoid residual double counting.

stages.label: Sponsor-approved specialty merchant
stages.detail: A 50-basis-point retained residual on $50,000 merchant volume produces $250. Model reserves, disputes, and service burden separately; higher yield does not establish higher profit.

stages.label: Exclusive-venue ATM withdrawals
stages.detail: A $3.00 surcharge less $1.25 combined venue and upstream shares retains $1.75 per withdrawal. Four thousand annual withdrawals retain $7,000 before operator servicing expenses.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Account Activation
diagrams.subtitle: Each failed check routes to a specific correction or a stopped submission.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values indicate check order, not risk scores. All four checks must pass for the relevant product; statutes, network contracts, and sponsor requirements impose distinct obligations.
diagrams.caption: Document evidence and the decision owner; never use alternate MIDs or product labels to bypass an adverse underwriting decision.

stages.label: Credit and debit pricing
stages.value: Pass: configure; fail: reprice and retest
stages.detail: Apply current Visa and Mastercard debit-surcharge prohibitions separately from 15 U.S.C. 1693o-2 and 12 CFR 235.7 routing rules. For New York, test displayed credit prices and surcharge limits against General Business Law section 518.

stages.label: ATM fee disclosure
stages.value: Pass: enable; fail: disable fee-bearing service
stages.detail: Under 12 CFR 1005.16, disclose the fee amount on screen or paper before commitment and obtain the consumer's election to continue. Preserve test evidence and confirm that cancellation avoids the fee.

stages.label: Service scope and cash custody
stages.value: Pass: document scope; fail: stop added services
stages.detail: Analyze actual services under 31 CFR 1010.100(ff); withdrawal-only operation does not by itself establish money-transmitter status. Added transmission or exchange services require separate classification and any applicable 31 CFR 1022.380 registration work.

stages.label: Sponsor underwriting and data controls
stages.value: Pass: activate; fail: remediate or decline
stages.detail: Verify sponsor acceptance, merchant category, applicable MATCH screening, reserves, PCI DSS responsibilities, and dispute exposure. Assess 15 U.S.C. 6801 and 16 CFR 314.3 where applicable; use Verifi RDR and Ethoca without suppressing required sponsor reporting.

diagrams.title: One Accountable Owner, Three Contract Specialists
diagrams.subtitle: The four-person Base pod expands to six people only in the Scaled case.
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT means full-time and C means contractor; contractor seats are people, not assumed full-time equivalents. Numeric values show Base seat occupancy: one for each active seat and zero for each Scaled-only addition. Sponsor personnel remain outside the pod.
diagrams.caption: Conservative and Base use 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C. Automation supports accountable operators rather than removing ownership.

stages.label: Owner and sponsor lead
stages.detail: Own pricing authority, sponsor relationships, placement contracts, cash controls, attrition review, and the annual owner-profit reconciliation; resolve exceptions raised by contractors.

stages.label: Merchant acquisition specialist
stages.detail: Maintain qualified cohorts, collect authorized statements, prepare accurate proposals, and negotiate venue introductions without promising sponsor acceptance or unsupported savings.

stages.label: Boarding and residual specialist
stages.detail: Operate IRIS CRM, reconcile Schedule A residuals, maintain boarding evidence, review Verifi RDR and Ethoca outcomes, and escalate unresolved disputes or reserve changes.

stages.label: ATM field-service specialist
stages.detail: Coordinate authorized replenishment, inspect terminals, respond to telemetry alarms, and reconcile service tickets against cash-custodian records without mixing vault cash and revenue.

stages.label: Portfolio operations lead
stages.detail: Add ownership of daily exception queues, merchant retention, sponsor reporting, and contractor quality when measured workload supports the Scaled six-person operating model.

stages.label: Dispute and support specialist
stages.detail: Add dedicated case handling, evidence collection, and merchant support; the resulting team totals two full-time people and four contractors, not six full-time employees.

diagrams.title: Allocate Startup Cash Without Counting Vault Cash
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets reconcile to $8,000 lean, $25,000 working, and $45,000 expanded.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values encode the $25,000 working plan. Each value string also specifies lean and expanded allocations, in that order. These are alternative budgets, not cumulative spending rounds. Leased or venue-owned terminals and separately supplied vault cash are assumed; operator-funded cash inventory needs additional capital.
diagrams.caption: Lean: $2,000 + $1,500 + $2,500 + $2,000 = $8,000. Working: $4,500 + $6,000 + $9,000 + $5,500 = $25,000. Expanded: $8,000 + $10,000 + $18,000 + $9,000 = $45,000.

stages.label: Contracting and operating setup
stages.detail: Fund entity setup, insurance deposits, sponsor onboarding, and review of residual ownership, termination, venue exclusivity, equipment responsibility, and cash-custody agreements.

stages.label: CRM and terminal deployment
stages.detail: Fund IRIS CRM configuration, residual import testing, telemetry setup, terminal lease deposits, connectivity, and installation; exclude any assumption of outright fleet purchase.

stages.label: Acquisition and pilot execution
stages.detail: Fund targeted outreach, site surveys, travel, demonstrations, and initial contractor work. Release spending against documented cohort progress rather than unverified transaction forecasts.

stages.label: Liquidity and service buffer
stages.detail: Hold operating cash for service incidents and residual payment lags; keep sponsor collateral separately identified. At Base fixed overhead, $5,500 covers approximately 1.1 months.

diagrams.title: The First 30 Days: Build Evidence Before Volume
diagrams.subtitle: Four weekly milestones prepare a defensible merchant and ATM pilot.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values indicate the final day of each milestone. The 30-day sprint prepares acquisition and operations; first deal timing remains 1–4 months, and the funnel spans an illustrative 120-day cohort rather than this sprint.
diagrams.caption: Finish the month with reviewed terms, a nested prospect cohort, tested controls, and a reconciled operating model.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Select sponsor and inspect contract economics
stages.detail: Owner compares Schedule A schedules, residual ownership, clawbacks, reserve terms, and supported categories. Deliver a written retained-revenue model and an ATM cash-custody plan.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Build qualified outreach and site evidence
stages.detail: Sales contractor creates the prospect register, requests authorized statements, and surveys suitable venues. Deliver stage definitions, pricing worksheets, and documented placement requirements without counting unsigned prospects as revenue.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Test boarding, pricing, and service controls
stages.detail: Operations contractor configures IRIS CRM and residual imports; field specialist tests telemetry and ATM fee disclosure. Record debit-pricing tests, dispute escalation ownership, and sponsor submission completeness.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.detail: Submit complete applications and negotiate placement terms. If accepted and installed, verify live results; otherwise record sponsor dependencies. Reconcile startup cash, fixed overhead, and all three canonical profit cases.
